chunks: Al-Husayn ibn Sa'id from Hammad and al-Nadr ibn Suwayd from al-Qasim ibn Sulayman from Ubayd ibn Zur'arah from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) who said:
The blood-money (diyah) is one thousand dinars, or twelve thousand dirhams, or one hundred camels. The basis in these two narrations is what he mentioned.
ai.seo_question: What is the prescribed amount of blood money (diyah) in Shia Islamic law?
ai.summary: This narration from al-Istibsar establishes the canonical valuation of blood-money (diyah) for a free Muslim, presenting three equivalent measures: 1,000 dinars, 12,000 dirhams, or 100 camels. The concluding phrase clarifies that this specific valuation serves as the definitive standard for reconciling apparent discrepancies in other related hadiths regarding compensation. This standardization reflects the Imami juristic approach to maintaining consistency in financial liabilities (diyah) across varying economic contexts.
